attributes.residual:
HOW THE .data BASE WAS DERIVED, since af_data_base_census could not resolve it: it printed `no target address resolvable from .text relocations` for .data and told the reader to fall back to config/GUNE5D/symbols.txt, which is exactly what decided it. Our object emits FOUR anonymous .data objects at offsets 0x000/0x080/0x0e8/0x170 with sizes 0x80/0x68/0x88/0x20 (@692, @3457, @3514, @3559 -- the do_ai dispatch table and three switch tables), and symbols.txt lists `jumptable_8011C0EC` 0x80, `jumptable_8011C16C` 0x68, `jumptable_8011C1D4` 0x88, `jumptable_8011C25C` 0x20 consecutively. The four sizes agree in order and sum to 0x190, and our @3559 at offset 0x170 lands exactly on jumptable_8011C25C, which is what makes the base 0x8011C0EC decidable rather than plausible. `jumptable_8011C27C` (0x80) is the next TU's and is outside the claim. The claim measured 100.0% bytes equal on the first build, so the derivation is confirmed by content, not only by size.

THE .bss CLAIM'S 4-BYTE SLACK IS STRUCTURAL. af_data_base_census's paste-ready line ends at 0x8025758C (our object's 0x678C), and dtk REFUSES it: `Split game/enemy/enemy.c .bss (0x80250E00..0x8025758C) ends within symbol 'gEnemies' (0x80251C18..0x80257590)`. Ending at 0x80257590 splits cleanly and datadiff downgrades the row from FLIP BLOCKER to `DATA-DEBT -- bss claim slack`, advisory, no DOL bytes. Quote the refusal, not the census line, when writing this claim.

THE REMAINING .sdata2 BLOCKER IS NOT A MISSING CLAIM, and this is the half of BLOCKER 3 the audit's framing gets wrong. Our object emits 34 anonymous .sdata2 pool objects totalling 0x10C. Pairing our .text relocations against the target's (af_data_base_census, 172 offset-shifted pairs, 24 unpaired) resolves each of them to a target address, and the addresses SPAN 0x80346810..0x803469B8, roughly 0x1A8 bytes -- a range enemy.c's source references PARTLY through those anonymous literals and PARTLY through named `extern f64 lbl_803468xx;` declarations it never defines. A TU's section is contiguous in the link, so enemy.c owns the whole run; our object under-emits it by about 0x9C bytes because ~19 of the constants are spelled as named externs instead of literals. No splits.txt line can fix that: closing this blocker means converting those extern references into literals so MWCC pools them, in the target's first-use order, and only then claiming the range. That is a distinct piece of work, it is the winglobals sdata2 pool-order problem (claim.law pool creation-order family), and it is the ONLY data blocker enemy.c has left.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: `python tools/gdl/composed_census/af_data_base_census.py game/enemy/enemy` reporting a SINGLE consistent .sdata2 base rather than the current 16 candidate bases would mean the pool already lines up and only a claim is missing -- which would refute this record's diagnosis outright.
hypothesis.count_consequence: count-neutral for .text: replacing a named-extern constant read with a literal keeps the same instruction word and changes only the relocation's symbol.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes -- the census at f2ce366f5 prints 16 mutually inconsistent candidate bases for .sdata2 (0x80346768, 0x80346798, 0x803467F0, 0x80346800, 0x80346808, 0x80346810, 0x80346818, 0x80346820, 0x80346830, 0x80346878, 0x80346880, 0x80346890, 0x80346898, 0x803468A0, 0x803468A8, 0x803468B0) against a single agreed base for .bss, and `Select-String config/GUNE5D/splits.txt '\.sdata2\s+start:0x8034'` returns no claim anywhere in 0x80346xxx, so the range is unclaimed and free.
hypothesis.statement: Close .sdata2 by converting enemy.c's named-extern FP constant references in 0x80346810..0x803469B8 into literals, in target first-use order, then claim the range. Order the work off the per-@N target addresses this run derived: the pairing already says which of our 34 pool entries belongs at which target address, so the 19 unemitted constants are exactly the addresses in that span with no @N mapped to them, and their VALUES are readable straight out of the retail DOL at those addresses.
